basis: Scaly inflammatory disease of the scalp and facial skin; no defined systemic immune mechanism.
Isolated defective spermatogenesis and sperm morphology affect reproduction without established endocrine dysfunction.
Cerebellar and pyramidal dysfunction define disease. Bladder dysfunction (9/24) and nystagmus reflect neural dysfunction; cirrhosis occurs in only 2/12.
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid blood-cell malignancy; lymphoma also requires the immune mechanism axis.
Renal tubular electrolyte-handling disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic acidosis and hypertension.
Familial infantile myeloid leukemia affects marrow and circulating myeloid cells.
Autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease; oral mucosal ulceration occurs in 30-79%. Associated neoplasms are separate diseases.
Inherited degeneration of distal motor neurons or axons; muscle weakness and wasting result from denervation.
Skin/hair hypopigmentation and neurologic impairment define GS1; annotated retinopathy occurs in 80-99%. Immunodeficiency is absent; hyperlipidemia alone adds no organ damage.
Congenital femoral hypoplasia or aplasia with restricted hip and knee movement.
Dyskeratosis congenita combines marrow failure with diagnostic nail/skin abnormalities and oral leukoplakia. Pulmonary fibrosis affects a minority.
Proliferative lesion confined to breast ducts; breast has no axis.
The defining syndrome combines femoral epiphyseal dysplasia, high myopia and hearing impairment.
Retinal dystrophy, cerebellar/peripheral neurologic disease and pituitary hormone deficiencies define this PNPLA6 syndrome group.
Immune granulomas involve lungs in ~90%; uveitis and cutaneous lesions are annotated 30-79%. Hepatic dysfunction and cytopenias also annotated frequent, omitted at cap.
Clonal myeloid blasts occupy marrow and blood. Extramedullary gingival involvement is not established in at least 30%; secondary infections are separate.
Long-bone bowing defines disease; dermatitis 1/2, thrombocytopenia 1/2, PAH/heart failure 1/3. Respiratory distress alone does not establish intrinsic lung injury.
Surfactant protein C dysfunction causes intrinsic alveolar/interstitial lung disease. PAH occurs in only 2/17; recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
ABCA4-associated retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Eyelid malformations, spastic diplegia and developmental speech impairment define the deletion syndrome; unspecified genitourinary anomalies do not establish renal damage.
Unilateral vas deferens aplasia affects reproduction. Associated renal agenesis is not established here above the approximately 30% threshold.
Intrinsic skeletal myopathy with reducing bodies, weakness and contractures. Respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung disease.
Predominantly Bardet-Biedl phenotype with retinal dystrophy/obesity; renal disease ~50%, cognitive impairment ~50-60%. Polydactyly omitted at cap; isolated RP is a subtype.
Congenital cerebral white-matter underdevelopment produces disproportionate enlargement of the occipital ventricular horns.
RIPK1-mediated autoinflammation; anemia 5/5 and splenomegaly 7/12 support blood involvement; oral ulcers occur in 8/14. Hepatomegaly is below 30%.
